description: Machine-readable subsystem lifecycle records. Obligations grow with the status a subsystem claims; see 64_Documentation_Extension_Framework section 4. Enforced by tests/tooling/audit_subsystem_lifecycle.py. A record is a claim about what is documented, not a claim that the subsystem is correct.

subsystems.title: Dual-Time Picard--Jameson Momentum Solver
subsystems.note: Verified locally 2026-09-18 (measurement duct-poiseuille-picard-2026-09-18): laminar square-duct Poiseuille flow at second order on three grids. The same duct at dt = 1.0 exhausted the pseudo-time cap every step and finished 18% off in pressure gradient; page 24 section 8 now states that a step is only as accurate as its pseudo-time convergence.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when temporal order is measured, a curvilinear-grid case reproduces a known solution, and the periodic wall-bounded configuration is re-characterised at current HEAD.
subsystems.demotion_reason: The supported claim rested on one laminar square duct measured for spatial order only. Temporal order, a curvilinear grid, and the streamwise-periodic wall-bounded configuration - where pseudo-time convergence stalled when last measured - were never checked.

subsystems.title: Newton--Krylov Momentum Solver
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Documented to the supported bar: scope limits, configuration, monitors, failure reasons, validation coverage, restart seeding, and a complete reference. The unresolved question is production suitability - the solver is characterised on single-block cases within a narrow declared scope, and no campaign has run it at the sizes a supported claim implies.

scientific_verification.not_applicable: No validation campaign has been run against this path; that absence is what keeps the subsystem experimental rather than supported.

subsystems.title: Large-Eddy Simulation Subgrid Models

backward_compatibility.not_applicable: The legacy les: true / les: 1 / les: 2 shorthands remain accepted and are documented as spellings; nothing has been retired.

subsystems.note: Both defects that held this subsystem at known-defective are fixed. The dynamic procedure now forms the model tensor from the test filter of |S|S_ij, applies the deviatoric projection, and averages the Germano contractions over a selectable set; the constant model reads its coefficient from configuration every step and allocates no coefficient field. Status is experimental rather than supported because no reference-flow validation has been run: decaying isotropic turbulence with homogeneous averaging, where Cs(t) should settle near 0.16-0.17, is the check that would close the gap.

subsystems.title: RANS Turbulence Models

scientific_verification.not_applicable: The k-omega path produces no solution to verify: enabling it aborts the solver at the end of the first timestep, so no verification claim of any kind is made for it.

subsystems.note: Declared known-defective on 2026-09-18 after a code survey and a three-step run of the flat-channel case with k_omega enabled. Setup never allocates the K_Omega fields and FlowSolver's transport update is commented out, so the first UpdateSolverHistoryVectors call copies a null vector and PETSc aborts with a null-argument error at the end of step one. The previous record described the runtime update as incomplete; it was absent. The selector stays reachable, with the disclosure printed by picurv validate and run, so the path can be repaired in place and return to experimental.

subsystems.title: Wall Function Boundary Treatment

backward_compatibility.not_applicable: The wall_function block and its -wallfunction / -wall_roughness flags are unchanged; nothing has been renamed or retired.

subsystems.note: Separated from the RANS record because a wall function is configured independently of both LES and RANS, and because the RANS runtime update is incomplete while this treatment is separately usable. The velocity laws and their friction-velocity root-finds carry unit coverage, and the integration that applies them across the six faces is covered by tests/c/test_boundaries.c, which checks that the corrected first-interior velocity is the modelled profile at that cell's wall distance. Status is experimental rather than supported because no reference-flow comparison has been run and no shipped case enables it. All three laws are now reachable: the integration dispatches on the configured model rather than calling the log law unconditionally, and a channel run shows the three producing distinct friction velocities where the laws should differ and identical ones in the viscous sublayer, where every wall model must reduce to u+ = y+. The pass now records the friction velocity as the catalogued field `Utau` and writes near-wall statistics to <run.analysis.metrics>/wall_model.csv, including the first-cell y+ that says whether the selected law is being applied where it is valid; before that, u_tau was computed every step and discarded, so no wall diagnostic existed. Its storage was also allocated from the dof-3 DM while every reader opened it through the dof-1 DM, a pairing PETSc rejects, so enabling wall functions on a case with a WALL face aborted; tests/c/test_boundaries.c now allocates the way production does and compares the allocation against the field catalog descriptor, which is what makes that class of mismatch fail in the suite. A toy channel exercising all three laws end to end found two defects that unit coverage could not reach. Werner-Wengle reported one identical u_tau at every wall cell, because wall_function() used its Newton initial guess as the answer; it now uses the closed-form taw_Werner()/u_Werner_explicit() pair, which is the Werner-Wengle model proper - the profile integrated across the first cell inverts without any root-find, realising the no-inner-iteration property the model is chosen for. The earlier iterative helpers are retained, unwired, with the reasons recorded at their definitions: their branch threshold depends on the friction velocity being solved for, and their two branches invert different relations, so they reconstruct the pointwise profile only below y+ = 11.81. Separately, the friction-velocity storage was allocated inside the LES/RANS block, so enabling a wall model without either of them left ApplyWallFunction dereferencing a null vector; allocation is now gated on the wall model alone, which is what the schema has always said. All three laws now produce friction velocities that vary cell to cell and differ from one another at y+ ~ 10-14, and agree exactly at y+ ~ 1.4 where every wall model must reduce to u+ = y+. None of this is validation against a reference flow, which has still not been run. The modelled stress now actually reaches the momentum equation. The correction sets a velocity, and the viscous operator reaches the wall through a viscosity times a gradient, so with the subgrid viscosity zeroed at wall faces - correct for a wall-resolved run, backwards for a wall-modelled one - only the molecular fraction u+/y+ of the stress was delivered, about a fourteenth at y+ = 267. The wall pass now publishes an effective wall eddy viscosity that the viscous flux uses at that face instead, reported as nu_wall_over_nu_mean; a 30-step channel shows the solutions with and without it separating monotonically, so the term is live, though its effect on a developed flow is not established. Three pairings are now rejected before a run starts - a wall model with no turbulence model, and cabot or werner under RANS - and a first-cell y+ outside the selected law's range warns each sample and stops the run after ten consecutive ones, since that depends on the mesh and cannot be settled at validation time.

subsystems.title: Lagrangian Particle Transport
subsystems.note: Verified locally 2026-09-18: the Einstein relation to 0.17% (brownian-msd-2026-09-18), exact uniform drift (uniform-drift-2026-09-18), and 0.67% Trilinear interpolation error on TGV3D (tgv-interpolation-2026-09-18). Walls absorb diffusing particles; in the thin interpolation_test domain that removed 55% of the cloud by t = 2, which its README now states. The diffusivity-gradient drift was inconclusive at 40,000 particles (diffusivity-gradient-drift-2026-09-18); the Brownian generator was seeded from the wall clock until 2026-09-18 and is now seeded from models.physics.particles.random_seed plus the rank and restart step, so identical inputs on the same rank count repeat exactly (brownian-rng-seeded-from-configuration).
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when the gradient drift is measured with paired seeds, every seeding mode's placement is checked against its definition, and CornerAveraged interpolation is measured.
subsystems.demotion_reason: The supported claim covered free diffusion, uniform drift and Trilinear interpolation. The diffusivity-gradient drift was inconclusive, Surface and SurfaceEdges seeding and CornerAveraged interpolation carried no verification, and Volume and PointSource placement were only production exercised.

subsystems.title: Online Eulerian Field Statistics
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Documented to the supported bar, including checkpoint/restart continuation and window identity. The unresolved question is whether the derived statistics have been validated against a reference profile rather than only unit-tested for internal consistency.

user_selector.not_applicable: Nothing here is selectable yet; the page describes the design that would have to exist before any selector is added.

subsystems.title: Workspace Topology and Reusable Asset Lifecycle

backward_compatibility.not_applicable: The workspace layout, the asset store, and the fixed run tree were introduced together and replaced the configurable directory surface outright; there is no earlier workspace format to migrate from, and monitor io.directories is rejected rather than translated.

mpi_distributed_execution.not_applicable: Workspace discovery, asset publication, and run materialization all run in the Python conductor on one process before the solver launches; no rank-dependent behaviour or collective call is involved.

security_credentials.not_applicable: Imports and asset publication read and write local paths under the invoking user's own permissions; reference-mode imports store a path, never a credential.

subsystems.note: Content-addressed asset identity covers the normalized provider settings, the checksums of referenced files, and the PICurv build, so an unchanged input reuses its object and any change to an equation, grid configuration, imported field, inlet parameter, or generator selects a new one. Publication is all-or-nothing per invocation: providers build into an isolated temporary run layout and nothing is published unless every selected provider succeeds. Status is experimental rather than supported because the reuse and materialization paths carry unit coverage in tests/test_workspace_lifecycle.py and the migrated precompute coverage in tests/test_cli_smoke.py, but no campaign has exercised the store at the scale where reflink availability, object accumulation, and pruning policy start to matter, and nothing removes orphaned objects automatically: the explicit `picurv storage prune --assets --unused-locally` command (storage.management) is the only reclamation path, and it has not been exercised at campaign scale. The restart statistics-state selector that this record once listed belongs to post.field_statistics, whose continuation it controls.

subsystems.title: Run Storage Management

security_credentials.not_applicable: Remote access reuses the operator's existing rclone remote and credentials; PICurv stores only the remote name/path and never copies provider credentials into a workspace.

subsystems.promotion_rationale: Documented to the supported bar, including failure safety and restore. The unresolved question is operational: the offload/restore cycle has not been exercised against the owner's actual remote at campaign scale.

subsystems.title: Run Directory Containment Guard

user_selector.not_applicable: Run-owned directory names are fixed; there is no public selector.

backward_compatibility.not_applicable: The fixed workspace topology was introduced before compatibility guarantees; legacy monitor directory overrides are intentionally rejected.

mpi_distributed_execution.not_applicable: The guard runs on rank zero before the collective directory setup and aborts the whole job, so no rank-dependent behavior arises.

subsystems.note: Verified locally 2026-09-18 by tests/test_run_directory_containment.py in the full Python suite; no separate runtime check was run.

subsystems.title: Geometric Periodic Boundaries
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Documented to the supported bar. The unresolved question is the wall-bounded pseudo-time convergence behaviour, which page 54 records as previously observed and requiring re-characterisation at current HEAD. A supported claim should not sit above an open characterisation question.

subsystems.title: Logging and Runtime Observability

examples.not_applicable: Logging is configured per run in monitor.yml rather than per case, so it has no example family in 65_Example_Catalog. Every shipped example exercises it through whichever monitor profile the run selects, and the profiles in config/monitors/ - Standard_Output.yml for quiet production runs - are its reference configurations. An example case that existed to demonstrate logging would be demonstrating the monitor profile, which 09_Monitor_Reference already specifies directly.

numerical_method.not_applicable: Logging reports the solver's state and never participates in it. The dependency direction is one-way, as 13_Code_Architecture section 5 records: logging reads SimCtx, and no solver module depends on logging for a numerical result, so there is no numerical method here to specify.

scientific_verification.not_applicable: Nothing logging produces is a scientific claim of its own; it reports quantities the subsystems that compute them are separately accountable for. Its own contracts - level gating, allow-list behaviour, snapshot cadence, string conversion - are behavioural and are covered by tests/c/test_logging.c rather than by physical validation.

subsystems.note: Registered as its own subsystem because every other module reports through it while nothing depends on it for a result, which is exactly the shape that leaves a module unowned: before this record it appeared in no subsystem, no capability family, no contract, no freshness surface, and in neither src/guide.md nor the module map of 13_Code_Architecture, despite owning the console tier system, the runtime metric emitters, and the lifecycle of every file in <run.runtime_logs>. A change to what a user sees therefore tripped no staleness suspicion anywhere. Status is supported rather than experimental because the console contracts carry direct unit coverage in tests/c/test_logging.c and the configuration surface has been stable and user-facing across releases; the claim is about those behavioural contracts, not about the correctness of any quantity another subsystem hands it to print. Verified locally 2026-09-18 by unit-logging within make unit; no runtime behaviour was re-measured.

subsystems.title: Domain Definition: Grid Ingestion, Metrics, and Dimensionality
subsystems.note: Owns how the computational domain reaches the solver: the three grid ingestion modes, PICGRID validation and nondimensionalization, metric construction, DMDA partition hints, and the 2D row mask. Multi-block domains are a separate planned record (domain.multiblock) because nothing couples blocks; the grid generator's composed geometries are grid.generator, which feeds the grid_gen mode here. The 2D value is experimental: the row mask carries unit coverage in tests/c/test_solver_kernels.c but no end-to-end run shows that a 2D case reproduces a planar solution. Verified locally 2026-09-18: metric closure to 3.7e-15 on the curvilinear bent-channel file grid (curvilinear-gcl-2026-09-18); all three grid modes run in the smoke suite. The 2D value is not verified end to end.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when programmatic_c and grid_gen grids reproduce a known solution and a 2D case is shown to match its planar counterpart end to end.

subsystems.title: Multi-Block Domain Coupling

user_selector.not_applicable: models.domain.blocks is refused at validation for any value other than 1, and -nblk other than 1 is refused at setup, so nothing is selectable until the coupling exists.

subsystems.note: Recorded on 2026-09-18 when a code survey found that every inter-block exchange (Block_Interface_U) is commented out, so a multi-block case ran as isolated single-block solves. The switch had been accepted and page 12 advertised multi-block support; both are now corrected, and tests/c/test_setup_lifecycle.c and tests/test_config_regressions.py hold the refusal.

subsystems.title: Immersed Boundaries, Moving Bodies, and Moving Frames

user_selector.not_applicable: models.physics.fsi.immersed and moving_fsi are refused at validation when true, and -imm, -fsi, -rfsi, -mframe, -rframe, -mhv and -lv are refused at setup, so nothing is selectable until the implementation exists.

subsystems.note: Recorded on 2026-09-18. The switches were accepted before and each ran a different problem without saying so: immersed reconfigured the Poisson solve around a body that is never loaded (ibm_interpolation_advanced is called only from commented-out code and defined nowhere), moving_fsi was inert, and the passthrough-only -mframe/-rframe skipped the convective term. The dormant Poisson branch and the Nvert solid markers are retained for the implementation this record describes.

subsystems.title: Composed Grid Generator (grid.gen)
subsystems.note: Both geometries are production-exercised along their plainest path (every periodic_test case uses box; bent_channel uses sweep with an unshaped rectangle and default-axis straight/arc segments). The seven wall-segment kinds, the circle cross-section, scaled sweeps, and all six transforms carry unit coverage in tests/test_grid_generator.py only; no solve has been run on any of them.

subsystems.title: Eulerian Initial Conditions
subsystems.note: Owns the C-runtime field modes (Zero, Constant, Poiseuille), the target-field choice (Ucat or Ucont), and the file and generated providers staged by the conductor (ic.gen expression and spectral_random_velocity). Constant runs in the flat_channel example and in the smoke suite, and spectral_random_velocity in the decaying-isotropic-turbulence example, but no mode has been checked against the field it claims to produce - Poiseuille, which should be an exact steady solution, is the cheapest such check.

subsystems.title: Eulerian Field Source and Analytical Fields
subsystems.note: Selects where the Eulerian field comes from each step: solved (every flow example), loaded from a prior run's output (the particle-tracking restart path, covered by the smoke suite), or prescribed analytically (the particle verification family). The solver that runs when the source is 'solve' is owned by the momentum and pressure records, not this one. Verified locally 2026-09-18: ZERO_FLOW, UNIFORM_FLOW and TGV3D carried the particle measurements recorded that day, UNIFORM_FLOW also on a curvilinear grid; load runs in the smoke restart variants.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when the load source is shown to reproduce the field it loaded and every analytical solution type is measured against its closed form.

subsystems.title: Pressure-Poisson Projection and Multigrid

lifecycle_and_restart.not_applicable: The pressure solve keeps no state of its own across a restart: P is part of the committed checkpoint bundle the run lifecycle owns, and the correction Phi and every multigrid operator are rebuilt each step from the current grid and velocity.

subsystems.note: Runs in every solved case. Evidence is the RHS helper coverage in unit-poisson-rhs, the multigrid coarse-solve residual invariant asserted by smoke-driven-periodic at two rank counts, and every flow example; PoissonSolver_MG itself still lacks direct unit coverage, which page 25 records. The immersed pre-solve branch inside it is dormant and belongs to the planned immersed_boundary record. Verified locally 2026-09-18: the analytic duct pressure gradient at second order (duct-poiseuille-picard-2026-09-18) and the multigrid coarse-solve invariant at 4 and 10 ranks (smoke-driven-periodic). Found and fixed 2026-09-18: PoissonSolver_MG never read the KSP converged reason, so a NaN solve surfaced later as a momentum failure (3 levels on a 9-node grid did exactly that). A NaN or preconditioner failure now stops the run at the Poisson solve with a message naming the multigrid depth, and any other divergence except the iteration cap warns; page 25 states both. No regression test drives the fatal path.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when PoissonSolver_MG has direct coverage, the multigrid option variants are each exercised, and the fatal-failure path has a regression test.

subsystems.title: Boundary Conditions
subsystems.note: Owns the boundary grammar, the wall, inlet and outlet types, their handlers, and the prescribed-flow inlet sources including profile.gen. The periodic type and the three periodic handlers are co-listed here but owned by boundary.periodic, which carries its own open question; each value names its owner in capability_families.json. Verified locally 2026-09-18: noslip, prescribed_flow and conservation reproduce duct Poiseuille flow at second order (duct-poiseuille-picard-2026-09-18). Found: a generated prescribed_flow profile on a programmatic_c grid delivers about 2/n too much flux, 12% at 16 cells (programmatic-inlet-flux-2026-09-18, not-met); disclosed in the prescribed_flow entry.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when constant_velocity and parabolic are measured against their analytic profiles and the prescribed_flow flux error on programmatic grids is resolved.

subsystems.title: Particle Scalar Micromixing (IEM)

selection_guidance.not_applicable: IEM has no selector. It updates the particle scalar Psi on every particle every step whenever particles are active, with a fixed C_IEM of 2.0, and is bypassed only when a verification scalar profile overrides Psi; there is no alternative model to choose between.

scientific_verification.not_applicable: No verification of the mixing rate has been run: no test compares the Psi variance decay against the IEM analytic rate for a known turbulence time scale, which is the check that would support a supported claim.

subsystems.note: Separated from particles.transport because it is a physics model with its own unvalidated coefficient, while transport - search, interpolation, advection, diffusion - is supported. The Schmidt numbers in solver.yml scalar_transport set particle diffusivity and belong to transport.

subsystems.title: Prescribed Verification Sources
subsystems.note: Replaces a physical field with an analytic one so a particle kernel can be checked against an exact answer: a prescribed diffusivity for the drift examples, a prescribed scalar for scatter verification (src/verification_sources.c). Both are exercised by shipped examples, but no numerical acceptance threshold has been run and gated, so the examples are designed evidence rather than recorded evidence.

subsystems.title: Post-Processing Pipeline
subsystems.note: Owns the postprocessor executable's Eulerian and Lagrangian kernels, dimensionalization, VTK output, and the particle statistics pipeline. Derived field statistics and spectra are post-processing stages with their own records (post.field_statistics, post.spectra) because each carries its own open validation question. Verified locally 2026-09-18: msd against the Einstein relation (brownian-msd-2026-09-18). Found and fixed 2026-09-18: q_criterion was accurate at cell centres but written at node positions and could not be nodal-averaged (q-criterion-tgv-2026-09-18, not-met); Qcrit is now a catalogued cell-centred field that nodal_average turns into Qcrit_nodal, which is the output name, and writing the cell-centred Qcrit is refused (q-criterion-nodal-tgv-2026-09-18, met). The msd reference point is the configured point source, so validation now refuses msd for a seeded case that does not use PointSource.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when normalize_field, specific_ke and nodal_average are measured on fields with known answers and dimensionalized output is checked against the reference scales.

subsystems.title: Turbulent Energy Spectra
subsystems.note: spectra.gen shell-spectrum and its conductor stage, plus summarize --plot-spectrum. Unit-tested in tests/test_spectra_shell_spectrum.py and tests/test_post_spectra_config.py and run by the decaying-isotropic-turbulence example; the spectrum has not been checked against an analytic input spectrum end to end.

subsystems.title: Run Monitoring, Diagnostics, and Inspection
subsystems.note: Owns everything in monitor.yml except logging and field statistics - physical-solution convergence monitoring, solver monitors, profiling, PETSc and memory diagnostics - and the read-only inspection surface: picurv summarize and plot.gen. Logging is observability.logging; field statistics are post.field_statistics. The four convergence modes are experimental: each is unit-tested, none has been checked against a run whose convergence state is known. Verified locally 2026-09-18: summarize reproduced the raw continuity, momentum, Poisson and convergence logs of a duct run and rendered a time-history plot; the steady_deterministic monitor reported the duct runs' steady state. Found and fixed 2026-09-18: the interpolation_error.csv time column was physical time multiplied by dt again; it now writes physical time, asserted in unit-logging.
subsystems.promotion_rationale: Promote when each convergence mode is run against a case whose convergence state is known and the profiling, memory and solver-monitor outputs are checked against the runs they describe.

subsystems.title: Run Execution, Validation, Checkpoints, and Restart
subsystems.note: Owns picurv run and validate, control-file generation, the committed checkpoint bundle, and every restart path (--continue, --restart-from, rank-change restart). Restart equivalence and rank-change restart are asserted by the smoke suite; restart is not bit-exact, at a characterized ~1e-7 floor that page 52 records. The run tree's containment guard is the separate run.directory_containment record; the inputs and assets a run consumes belong to workspace.asset_lifecycle; batch launch belongs to cluster.scheduling. Verified locally 2026-09-18: make smoke and smoke-mpi, including restart equivalence and restart across a changed rank count, and the walltime guard stopping a staged run at step 10 with a final checkpoint and clean exit inside its limit.

subsystems.title: Cluster Scheduling and Batch Execution
subsystems.note: Owns cluster.yml, run --cluster, submit, cancel (including --graceful), scheduler-script generation, and the warmup-and-extrapolate walltime guard. Slurm is the only scheduler. Covered by the conductor tests in tests/test_cli_smoke.py and production-exercised on the owner's cluster; submission itself cannot run in the local suite. Verified locally 2026-09-18 up to submission: run --cluster --no-submit staged correct sbatch scripts (resources, walltime export, identity check, srun layout), submit --dry-run chained post with afterok, and the walltime guard fired end to end. Slurm submission itself is not verified here. Held at experimental until a cluster run verifies what the local suite cannot reach: sbatch submission and its accounting, cancel and cancel --graceful against a live job, and the post job's afterok dependency firing.

subsystems.title: Parameter Sweeps and Studies
subsystems.note: Owns study.yml, picurv sweep (including --continue and --reaggregate), array-script generation, metric aggregation, and study plots. grid_independence is production-exercised by shipped studies; timestep_independence and sensitivity are experimental. Verified locally 2026-09-18: a shipped scatter study was staged with --no-submit, each case executed locally from its case index, and sweep --reaggregate filled every metric. Found and fixed: six shipped studies globbed metrics under logs/ while the runtime writes them to <run.analysis.metrics>, and the interpolation study named a file that does not exist. Array submission itself is not verified here. Held at experimental until a cluster run verifies the array job, max_concurrent_array_tasks throttling, and aggregation over cases that ran as array tasks.

subsystems.title: Case Templates and Initialization
subsystems.note: Owns picurv init, sync-config (including --overwrite and --prune, which rewrite or delete template-managed files), and status-source drift reporting. init is the first step of every tutorial and smoke run and works. Drafted as supported, then verified on 2026-09-18 and held at experimental: sync-config and status-source predate the workspace layout init now creates. On a fresh flat_channel workspace, status-source reported an edit to config/solver.yml as unmodified and nine template files as missing, because init renames template files into canonical config/ names and status-source compares by the original names; sync-config then copied the nine template files into the case root under their original names, duplicating the configuration outside config/ and never refreshing config/. Page 05 still documents both through a case-local ./my_case/picurv wrapper that init no longer creates.

subsystems.title: Build, Source, and Version Management
subsystems.note: Owns build, version, versions list/install/activate, source update, pull-source, per-run executable pinning, the job-start identity check, and workspace reproducibility.require_clean_release. Experimental because the version workflow is partly built - install and activate exist, later phases do not - and picurv source update has no test at all.

owner_decisions_note: A record carrying `proposed_status` is documented to that higher bar but still claims the lower one. The lifecycle gate checks documentation obligations against the proposal, so nothing is under-written; what it cannot check is production suitability or scientific correctness, which is why the promotion waits for the repository owner rather than being taken by the tooling.
